A_target.statement:
Let $X$, $Y$ be [[Definition:Topological Space|topological spaces]] with $x_0 \in X$, $y_0 \in Y$.
Then:
:$\map {\pi_1} {X \times Y, \tuple {x_0, y_0} } \cong \map {\pi_1} {X, x_0} \times \map {\pi_1} {Y, y_0}$

B_source.statement: A mapping $f: Z \to X \times Y$ is [[Definition:Continuous Mapping (Topology)|continuous]] {{iff}} $\pr_X \circ f$ and $\pr_Y \circ f$ are continuous.

substitutions.maps into the product: loops and homotopies in X x Y

object_map.reformulation: Use the universal property of the product to split loops and homotopies into components.

validity_conditions: The product must carry the product topology, which has exactly this universal property.
Concatenation of loops is defined componentwise, so the bijection respects the group operation.
proof_plan: By the source result, a loop $\gamma$ in $X \times Y$ at $\tuple {x_0, y_0}$ is the same as a pair of loops $\tuple {\pr_X \circ \gamma, \pr_Y \circ \gamma}$.
Likewise, a homotopy $H: \closedint 0 1^2 \to X \times Y$ is the same as a pair of homotopies.
